Updated Tue, Nov 10, 4:32 AM. Players ruled out on the injury report are removed; questionable players are flagged. Check final inactives before kickoff.

Fair odds
The price that matches our probability. In testing on 2022 through 2026, our top 5 players each week scored 58.5% of the time, and our percentages matched how often players actually scored. The model averages five fits so one random draw can't move the board.

Book
The best anytime-TD price at DraftKings or FanDuel when we last checked. Books keep a cut of roughly 20% on these bets, so compare our chance with the book's chance after the cut, not the raw price.

Top 5
Our five most likely scorers. In testing on 2022 through 2026 they scored 58.5% of the time, against 53.7% for the top 10. Graded as their own tier on the record page.

Value 5
Up to five players with a 20% chance or better, priced from +150 to +400, whose best book price pays at least 5 cents per $1 more than our probability says it should. These lose more often than the Top 5 but pay more when they hit. We haven't been able to test this against past prices, so each pick is locked at kickoff and graded at the price we picked it, 1 unit each. Prices move; check your book before betting.

Favorable / Neutral / Tough
Half how many points Vegas expects the team to score, half the defense: touchdowns, yards and red-zone looks it allows to the position, red-zone trips and touchdown rate it allows, and how efficient offenses are against it on runs (RBs, QBs) or passes (WRs, TEs). Favorable is the top quarter of this week's players at the position, tough the bottom quarter. In 2022–2026, favorable players scored 23% of the time and tough ones 15%. Our probability already includes all of this; the tag shows which way the matchup leans.

Red-zone touches
Targets plus carries inside the opponent's 20-yard line, per game over the player's last 8 games.

Matchup
Touchdowns this defense allowed to the position over its last 8 games, compared with the league average. See all matchups.

name: methodology
title: How Probable Makes Its Picks | Probable
description: What goes into Probable's game projections and touchdown picks, how they are tested, and how picks are graded.
text:
probable

HOW IT WORKS

How Probable picks

What goes into our touchdown picks and game projections, how we test them, and what the tests say.

Where the data comes from

Every number starts with public NFL play-by-play data from the nflverse project: every snap since 2019, who got the ball, where on the field, and what it was worth. We add weekly rosters, the official injury report and each game's scheduled starting quarterback. Sportsbook lines come from DraftKings and FanDuel.

The models re-run Tuesday, Thursday, Friday after the final injury report, Saturday and Sunday morning.

Touchdown picks

For every quarterback, running back, receiver and tight end, we estimate the chance they score a rushing or receiving touchdown. Passing touchdowns don't count. The model looks at:

Volume: targets and carries per game, and their share of the team's.
Red zone: touches inside the 20, 10 and 5, and their share of goal-line carries.
Team scoring: how many points Vegas expects the team to score.
Matchup: touchdowns the defense has allowed to that position recently.
Track record: how often the player has scored, adjusted for small samples.

Players ruled out on the injury report are removed. In testing on 8,836 player-games from 2025–2026 the model never trained on, 60.0% of each week's top 10 scored. The percentages are realistic: players we gave about a 30% chance scored about 30% of the time. Most volume and red-zone value is already priced in by sportsbooks, and we haven't yet tested the model against sportsbook TD prices, so treat our fair odds as a reference, not a signal to bet. Books keep a cut of roughly 20% on anytime-TD bets.

Game projections

Each game's projected score comes from team offense and defense efficiency (EPA per play and success rate, split into passing and running) from every play this season and last, weighted toward recent games. We then adjust for:

Starting quarterback: his recent value per dropback, with backups and rookies starting near backup level. A team starting someone other than its usual quarterback is flagged.
Rest, home field and division games.
Weather and roof for the projected total.

Tested on 2021-2025 seasons, each predicted by a model trained only on earlier seasons: our projected margin missed the final by 10.09 points on average, against 9.76 for the Vegas closing line. We picked 65.1% of winners; taking the Vegas favorite every time picked 66.5%.

Why we don’t make spread or over/under picks

Against the spread, our projections went 49.6% in testing. You need about 52.4% to break even at standard -110 odds. Betting only the games where we disagreed with Vegas the most didn't help either. Closing lines already reflect quarterback news, so public data rarely beats them.

We'd rather tell you that than dress up a coin flip as a lock. Our line is shown next to Vegas's as a second opinion, and spread picks will only return if a model beats closing lines in testing.

Where our line helps: before the market moves

Closing lines are hard to beat, but opening lines are softer. From 2021 to 2026, when our projection disagreed with the opening spread, the line moved toward our number by kickoff about two times in three (65–72%, depending on the size of the gap), and this held in games with no quarterback news. That is called closing line value, and it is the earliest sign that a number has real information in it.

We now save each game's opening and closing line from DraftKings and FanDuel and grade this live on the Model Performance page. The home page lists the games where we disagree with Vegas most, with how far the line has moved since it opened. Until the live record backs it up, these are second opinions, not picks.

How picks are graded

Each game and player uses the last projection we published before kickoff. Updates made after a game starts never count. Touchdown picks are graded on whether each of the week's top 10 scored. Game projections are graded on whether the projected winner won.

The Record page shows every graded week.

What we don’t claim

A projection isn't a guarantee, and a model that tested well can still have a bad week. Nothing here is betting advice. If you bet, bet what you can afford to lose. If gambling stops being fun, call or text 1-800-GAMBLER.
